promised.clause: every write accepted before it survives a crash
promised.detail: Successful sync() makes all previously accepted writes in every live WAL generation survive a crash, provided the OS, filesystem and device honor their persistence contract.

promised.clause: all or nothing, one WAL record
promised.detail: A write batch publishes and recovers all its mutations together, without exposing a partial batch.

promised.clause: unmoved by later writes and compactions
promised.detail: A captured snapshot keeps its logical view across later writes, flushes and compactions.

promised.clause: the engine refuses writes until reopened
promised.detail: A failed WAL sync poisons the engine and blocks further mutations until a successful reopen of valid on-disk state.
WAL records, SST blocks and new versioned MANIFEST envelopes use CRC-32 checksums; legacy unversioned MANIFESTs upgrade on their next install.

promised.clause: a real past state, every synced write in it
promised.detail: Under the simulated device model, recovered state equals some prefix of acknowledged writes that includes every successfully synced write.

promised.clause: reported when a later sync mark proves it
promised.detail: Recovery reports corruption without modifying the WAL when a surviving later sync marker with the readable header's private nonce proves damaged bytes were synced; without that proof damage truncates, and deliberate nonce forgery is outside the threat model.

promised.clause: old log synced before the next opens
promised.detail: Rotation syncs the closed WAL generation before creating the next, so generations become durable in order.

not_promised.clause: lost if the machine goes down
not_promised.detail: A successful put() or delete() before sync() may be lost after a crash.
Dropping a handle does not acknowledge crash durability.
Concurrent access by two independent processes to one directory is not validated as a supported usage; the OS lock rejects a second owner.
Power loss is simulated with torn writes, directory durability and per-file loss; these suites do not establish behavior on physical hardware.
The API and storage format may change before 1.0.

not_built.clause: compression, range deletes, reverse iteration, transactions

bugs_found.title: Torn unsynced WAL tail rejected as corruption
User values could mimic a sync marker (found before merge)
Cross-generation WAL prefix violation on rotation

roadmap.title: Storage API: reverse/prefix scans, namespaces, range deletes, TTL

examples.python:
from kiban import Kiban

with Kiban(directory) as db:
    db.put("hello", "world")
    db.sync()
    assert db.get("hello") == b"world"
    with db.snapshot() as snapshot:
        db.put("hello", "later")
        assert snapshot.get("hello") == b"world"
    db.batch([("put", "a", "1"), ("put", "b", "2")])
    assert list(db.scan("a", "c")) == [(b"a", b"1"), (b"b", b"2")]
